requirements.requirement: eth1 (node2 segment) and eth2 (node3 segment) configured as untagged access ports on node1, each in its own separate VLAN
requirements.summary: bridge vlan add commands set eth1 to VLAN 101 PVID untagged and eth2 to VLAN 102 PVID untagged; bridge vlan show confirms this both immediately after configuration and after node1's reboot (config reapplied via systemd oneshot unit).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 remain isolated from one another (separate VLANs/subnets, no cross-VLAN forwarding)
requirements.summary: Cross-subnet pings between node2 (192.168.101.2) and node3 (192.168.102.2) fail with 'Destination Net Unreachable' both before and after all three nodes were rebooted; ip_forward on node1 was explicitly set to 0 and confirmed 0 post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: node1 keeps a working link to each host inside its own VLAN
requirements.summary: node1's Bridge.101/Bridge.102 SVIs (192.168.101.1, 192.168.102.1) successfully ping node2 and node3 respectively, and vice versa, both pre- and post-restart. A benign DUP! ICMP artifact was observed and investigated, attributed to the nested-virtualization dataplane rather than VLAN misconfiguration, and did not affect 0% packet loss.

requirements.requirement: node1 restart resilience: VLAN/bridge/SVI configuration and connectivity/isolation survive a node1 reboot
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline captured (boot_id ce04f497...), reboot acknowledged and connection reset observed, new boot_id (c26dac0f...) confirms restart, and the new systemd oneshot unit (vlan-access-segmentation.service) reapplied the Bridge/VLAN/SVI state at boot; connectivity to node2/node3 and isolation between them were reconfirmed afterward.

requirements.requirement: node2/node3 restart resilience: static IP configuration and isolation/connectivity survive reboot
requirements.summary: Both hosts' static IPs were made persistent via NetworkManager 'Wired connection 2' profiles (autoconnect=yes); pre-restart boot_id, restart acknowledgement, and changed post-restart boot_id were captured for each node, with connectivity to node1 and isolation from each other reconfirmed afterward.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the core task: eth1 and eth2 on node1 (SONiC) were configured as untagged/PVID access ports in separate VLANs (101 and 102) using the kernel vlan-aware Bridge device, since the ASIC-backed Ethernet* ports were unusable on this SONiC-VS platform. node1 retains a working L3 presence in each VLAN via Bridge.101/Bridge.102 SVIs, confirmed reachable from node2 and node3 respectively. node2 and node3 are demonstrably isolated from each other (different subnets, ip_forward disabled), both before and after a full one-at-a-time reboot of all three nodes, with boot-identity changes, restart acknowledgements, and post-restart recovery of VLAN state, IP configuration, connectivity, and isolation directly observed for every node. A cosmetic duplicate-ICMP-reply artifact was investigated and reasonably attributed to the nested-virtualization dataplane rather than the VLAN configuration. Minor hygiene concerns: an offload-disabling change (GRO/GSO/TSO off) made during troubleshooting was not explicitly reverted, though it was very likely nullified by node1's later reboot; a temporary service mask was promptly undone.
limitations: Whether the ethtool -K offload changes on eth1/eth2 (cmd-6abaed333e0a4236) persisted after node1's reboot was not directly re-verified in the captured trace; it is inferred (not confirmed) to have reset because runtime-only ip/bridge state on this SONiC-VS platform does not survive reboot and the persistence unit does not reapply ethtool settings.

The fixed lifecycle 'after_prepare' snapshot is an alias of 'before_prepare' (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison rather than a genuine after-prepare baseline.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were directly connected to the task (bridge/VLAN configuration, SVI creation, persistence via systemd unit and NetworkManager profiles) or to the mandated restart-evidence protocol, and diagnostic commands (tcpdump, arping, ethtool status, dmesg, nmcli/firewall-cmd status, iptables/nft listing) were read-only. Two mutations stand out as not clearly tied to a task outcome: (1) cmd-6abaed333e0a4236 disabled GRO/GSO/TSO offloads on eth1/eth2 while chasing a benign duplicate-ICMP cosmetic artifact that the executor itself later concluded was unrelated to VLAN configuration and caused by the nested-virtualization dataplane -- this was never explicitly reverted, though it was likely reset by node1's subsequent reboot since ethtool runtime settings do not persist and the persistence unit does not reapply them (unconfirmed). (2) cmd-31e0d925cdac4545 masked interfaces-config.service; this was promptly and fully reverted via cmd-30d9d08cb50e4682 (unmask), a bounded low-risk action. Docker0 IP/interface cleanup (cmd-f3ef99a8bc014532) was framed as following the SONiC reference runbook for a pre-existing class-E leak and is not evidence of executor-caused residue.
